audit.why: 57.52% over 904 games — the best matchup in my slice. A dashless mage against the strongest point-and-click level 1 in the game, and the content win[] array reflects it honestly at four stages to two.
Spike placement is right — your levels 1-3, her two-item artillery timing. What was wrong was which ability owns her threat window, not when the window is.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings — spikes[3], mid, late, whys[6] and wants.foe[1] — say Mel's ULTIMATE reflects your burst back at you. It does not. Rebuttal, her W, is the reflect.
audit.why: Riot's Rebuttal text: 'Mel forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed.' Golden Eclipse is a global strike on Overwhelm-marked enemies with no reflect in it at all. Getting this wrong costs the player the matchup twice over. First, it aims his patience at the wrong cooldown: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s, the longest basic cooldown in either kit, while Golden Eclipse is 120s — so 'wait out her ult before committing' points at the wrong clock. Second, and worse, it hides the actual rule: Rebuttal reflects PROJECTILES. Comet Spear and Grand Starfall are both projectiles and come straight back at you. Shield Vault is a targeted dash, not a projectile, so it goes through. The correct instruction is the exact opposite of what the page implies — you open on Rebuttal with the stun, not the spear.
audit.corrected: The reflect moved to Rebuttal in all five places, with the projectile rule and the 38s cooldown stated, and Shield Vault named as the safe opener.

audit.whatIsWrong: Searing Brilliance and Overwhelm are never mentioned, so the page cannot explain what her ultimate actually does.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse 'strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her, dealing additional damage for each stack of Overwhelm'. Overwhelm comes from her damaging you. So refusing her chip is not just health preservation, it directly reduces the size of a global execute you cannot dodge or walk out of. The page instead describes her ult as a lane-range reflect.

edits.before: Mel's threat window — her R reflects your committed W-Q-R burst back at you, and from full build she pokes and executes you before you close the gap.
edits.after: Mel's threat window — Rebuttal reflects your Comet Spear and Grand Starfall straight back, and Golden Eclipse reaches you anywhere you carry Overwhelm.

edits.after: Time Rebuttal so your own spear and Starfall land on you instead

edits.after: Face Aegis Assault at Radiant Volley, then open on Rebuttal with Shield Vault

edits.before: Full-build Mel out-ranges your Q, executes you with W/E, and reflects your committed W-Q-R with her ult — she reclaims the lane decisively, so play safe and end before this.
edits.after: Full-build Mel outranges Comet Spear, Rebuttal reflects the spear back at you, and Golden Eclipse hits every Overwhelm stack she has put on you from anywhere on the map.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you stay in control: empowered-Q poke and E-blocks let you sit on her while she can only chip back. The one real trap is her R — if you dump your full W-Q-R into her while it is up, she reflects it, so bait or wait out her ult before you commit the all-in. At 6, Grand Starfall is your map weapon more than a lane finisher: use the lead you built to leap on a sidelane and snowball the game elsewhere while she is stuck farming.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 you stay in control: empowered Comet Spear and Aegis Assault let you sit on her while she chips back. The real trap is Rebuttal, not her ult — it reflects projectiles, so your spear and your Starfall both come back at you, while Shield Vault is a targeted dash and goes straight through. Open on it with the stun. It is 38s at rank 1, the longest basic cooldown in the lane, so once she spends it she is defenceless. At 6, use Grand Starfall on a sidelane.

edits.before: This is where it flips hard. By 2+ items Mel is a full-build artillery mage — she out-ranges your Q, pokes you down before you can W-in, and her R can wall off and reflect your one committed burst. Your damage has plateaued while hers scales. So everything must be front-loaded: get the lead before her items, end the game off your roams, and never walk into her poke-execute range from even HP in the late game.
edits.after: This is where it flips. By 2+ items Mel outranges Comet Spear and pokes you down before Shield Vault reaches, Rebuttal sends your projectiles back, and Golden Eclipse is global — it strikes every Overwhelm stack she has put on you no matter where you stand. That is why refusing her chip matters: fewer stacks is a smaller ult. Front-load everything, take the lead before her items, and never sit at even health in her range.

notes: THE FINDING: five separate strings said Mel's ULTIMATE reflects your burst. It does not — Rebuttal (W) is the reflect, and Riot's text is explicit that it 'reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker'. Golden Eclipse has no reflect in it whatsoever. This mattered in two ways. It aimed the player's patience at the wrong cooldown, since Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s and Golden Eclipse is 120s, and it buried the rule that actually decides the all-in: Comet Spear and Grand Starfall are both projectiles and are reflected, while Shield Vault is a targeted dash and is not. The page implied you should hold your combo; the correct play is to open THROUGH Rebuttal with the stun. Also added Overwhelm: Golden Eclipse scales with the stacks she has already put on you and hits from anywhere on the map, so refusing her poke shrinks an undodgeable ult.
